extracted.intended_audience: USPTO leadership, patent and trademark examiners/attorneys, agency staff, and IP stakeholder community (practitioners, PPAC/TPAC, policymakers)
extracted.subtask_description: Agency-level standards and procedural requirements covering fee reviews and rulemaking, operational/asset/energy/security management, examiner and attorney training programs, and mandated workload reporting relevant to patent and trademark operations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Civil monetary penalty inflation adjustment
rubrics_metrics.description: Under the Federal Civil Penalties Inflation Adjustment Act of 1990, as amended by the 2015 Improvements Act, agencies are required to make regular and consistent inflationary adjustments of civil monetary penalties to maintain their deterrent effect.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Agencies must periodically adjust penalties for inflation; the USPTO reported no civil monetary penalties assessed during FY 2021.

rubrics_metrics.name: Biennial review of user fees (Chief Financial Officers Act)
rubrics_metrics.description: The Chief Financial Officers Act requires a biennial review of agency fees, rents, and other charges imposed for services provided to specific beneficiaries to identify such activities and begin charging fees or periodically adjust existing fees.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Objective is to minimize general taxpayer subsidy by aligning fees to current costs or market value. The USPTO conducts biennial reviews, uses activity-based costing to calculate costs per activity, and assesses fees at least biennially.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fee-setting to recover full cost
rubrics_metrics.description: When appropriate, USPTO fees are adjusted to be consistent with legislative requirements to recover the full cost of the goods or services provided to the public.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: USPTO is a fully fee-funded agency; uses activity-based costing to calculate cost of activities performed for each fee, and adjusts fees to promote operational efficiency, align fees with costs, and ensure adequate revenue.

rubrics_metrics.name: Stakeholder engagement in fee rulemaking
rubrics_metrics.description: Fee proposals and adjustments must be developed with stakeholder input via PPAC/TPAC, public hearings, notices of proposed rulemaking (NPRMs), and consideration of public comments prior to final rules.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: FY 2017 comprehensive fee review led to an initial patent fee proposal shared with PPAC and public; public hearing held (Sept 6, 2018); NPRM published (July 31, 2019); comments were reviewed before finalizing adjustments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mandatory electronic filings (operational integrity)
rubrics_metrics.description: Implementation of mandatory electronic filings (effective February 2020) as part of a broader ERM framework to improve the effectiveness of operations and preserve the integrity of the Trademark Register.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Mandatory e-filing increases the USPTO's ability to address improper behavior and is part of data-driven operational controls.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of data analytics to detect improper filings
rubrics_metrics.description: USPTO leverages data analytics capabilities to identify and mitigate the impact of improper behavior in trademark filings and has begun analyzing patent filings for signs of improper activity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Advanced analytical methodologies and greater data processing capacity are being applied as part of the ERM framework to ensure integrity and prestige of registers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Optimize workspace and reduce agency footprint
rubrics_metrics.description: The USPTO pursues returning leased space and other measures to 'reduce the footprint' to save rent and reduce environmental impact.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: Returned Carlyle Place leased space saving 55,159 sq ft and ~$2.1M annual rent; clearing space ahead of schedule saved estimated annual rent of $468,000.

rubrics_metrics.name: Data center and facility infrastructure resilience
rubrics_metrics.description: Enhance and modernize data center heating, cooling, fire suppression, electrical systems, independent chillers, backup generator, server reconfiguration, and conversion to pre-action dry fire suppression.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Upgrades intended to protect critical infrastructure with independent systems separate from base building systems.

rubrics_metrics.name: Physical security upgrades for facilities
rubrics_metrics.description: Improve physical security at building entrances and for security staff (e.g., construction of bollards, ballistic shields at security guard desks), plus upgrades to security access control systems.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Projects completed in FY 2021; security enhancements also include communications upgrades (see emergency radio communications).

rubrics_metrics.name: Pandemic-related facility health and safety protocols
rubrics_metrics.description: Maintain increased cleaning frequency of high-touch areas, provide hand sanitizer and sanitizing wipes, and follow CDC guidance for social distancing for onsite health activities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: flu shot campaigns and on-campus blood donations resumed with CDC-compliant protocols; availability of sanitizer at elevator lobbies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Renewable energy procurement (Energy Policy Act compliance)
rubrics_metrics.description: Support the Energy Policy Act of 2005 requirement to purchase at least 7.5% of total electricity consumption from renewable sources.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: USPTO purchased 6,600 MWh of RECs (1 REC = 1 MWh), which exceeded 10% of annual energy consumption in FY 2020.

rubrics_metrics.name: Energy efficiency measures
rubrics_metrics.description: Implement energy efficiency improvements to reduce overall energy consumption (e.g., LED lamp replacements, engagement with lessors for building improvements).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: Replaced ~34,000 T-8 fluorescent lamps with 12-watt LEDs across campus, saving ~3,100,994 kWh (4.7% of consumption) and extending lamp life by ~20,000 hours per lamp.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fleet and telework emissions reductions
rubrics_metrics.description: Adopt fuel-efficient and hybrid vehicles in the fleet and support teleworking to reduce commuting emissions and local congestion.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Converted five fleet vehicles to GSA E85/hybrid; telework (mandatory/maximum since March 2020) reduced emissions substantially (reported reductions in tons of emissions).

rubrics_metrics.name: Waste diversion and recycling targets and practices
rubrics_metrics.description: Pursue waste diversion and recycling to reduce landfill waste and promote reuse (including recycling/donating furniture/electronics, energy-from-waste transfers).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: FY 2021: achieved 35% waste diversion at Alexandria campus with zero trash to landfill; transferred 656 tons of nonhazardous solid waste to an Energy-from-Waste Facility.

rubrics_metrics.name: Asset management modernization (RFID & process streamlining)
rubrics_metrics.description: Track agency assets (nearly 125,000) and modernize verification processes using radio frequency electronic identification (RFID) and cyber discovery tools to reduce custodial workload.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Improvements included increasing RFID identification rate to over 80%, reducing property custodians from 807 to 320, decreasing certification inventories from four to two per year, updating reports to show only assets not seen by discovery tools.

rubrics_metrics.name: Surplus property disposal via GSAXcess and reuse
rubrics_metrics.description: Interface USPTO asset management system with GSAXcess for electronic transfer and disposal of excess/surplus property, promoting reuse or transfer to other agencies, schools, public auctions, or recycling.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Goal is to preserve environment, protect resources, and generate revenue. Example: recovered $36,001 through a GSA auction in FY 2021.

rubrics_metrics.name: Records disposition and destruction compliance
rubrics_metrics.description: Relocate, transfer, or destroy agency records and materials in accordance with records management requirements and National Association of Information Destruction (NAID) standards.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: relocation of plant and trademark documents to archival facilities; destruction of pallets of documents and microfilm with Certificates of Destruction per NAID requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Procurement strategies for cost efficiency (leasing, consolidation, JIT)
rubrics_metrics.description: Adopt procurement approaches such as leasing copiers, consolidating supply procurement, and just-in-time (JIT) fulfillment to reduce overhead, inventory, and costs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Leasing copiers reduces overhead and simplifies operations; consolidation of TEAP supplies and JIT fulfillment eliminated inventory and saved over $100,000.

rubrics_metrics.name: Employee background investigations support
rubrics_metrics.description: Support background investigation initiatives (e.g., National Background Investigations Bureau) by releasing required investigation actions for employees.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: USPTO released approximately 2,000 investigation actions during the fiscal year to support employee vetting.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mandatory in-house Patent Law and Evidence training for GS-12 examiners
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide a mandatory in-house Patent Law and Evidence course for all GS-12 patent examiners covering authoritative court decisions on 35 U.S.C. §§ 101, 102, 103, and 112 and evidence handling during examination.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Course ensures consistent application of statutory issues and evidentiary handling across examiners.

rubrics_metrics.name: Patent Corps Examination Training (consistency in examination policy)
rubrics_metrics.description: Deliver mandatory or elective Patent Corps courses designed to bring consistency to application of patent examination policy, practice, and procedures across technologies.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Courses include Case Law Review (Federal Circuit and Supreme Court decisions) and other topical trainings; cumulative mandatory training hours reported (approx. 50,358 in FY 2021).

rubrics_metrics.name: Patent Examiner Refresher Training Program
rubrics_metrics.description: Optional program for examiners with at least one year experience to take refresher courses to keep current on procedures, legal matters, communication, and automation relevant to their specialty.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Refresher courses cover evolving knowledge, skills, and abilities; program reports number of trainings, participants, and total hours (e.g., Patent Law and Evidence: 238 trainings, 11,003 participants, 19,330 hours).

rubrics_metrics.name: Master Class Program for experienced examiners
rubrics_metrics.description: Optional deeper-dive program for examiners with at least one year experience to study specific advanced topics beyond refresher offerings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Topics include AIA Declarations of Attribution or Prior Public Disclosure, CPC, and Examination of Ranges; FY 2021 totals provided (e.g., 34 trainings, 1,283 participants, 1,576 hours).

rubrics_metrics.name: Patent Examiner Technical Training Program (PETTP)
rubrics_metrics.description: Program that brings scientists, engineers, designers, and other external experts to teach examiners about technological advances, emerging trends, and innovations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Enables subject-matter experts from industry and academia to present (virtually or onsite); FY 2021 totals: 524 events, 37,626 hours, 26,775 examiner participants, average 4.6 hours per examiner.

rubrics_metrics.name: Site Experience Education
rubrics_metrics.description: Program to provide examiners education in technology at source sites (visits to innovation sites) to receive updates and view technologies first-hand.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: COVID-19 affected travel; USPTO explored online technical conferences and virtual tours as alternatives; example collaboration with Olympus for a virtual lecture and tour.

rubrics_metrics.name: Aspiring Managers Program (AMP) and leadership development
rubrics_metrics.description: Cohort-based five-month program combining assessments, classroom training, workshops, shadowing, and mentoring to develop leadership and technical skills for managerial roles in Patents.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Incorporates all 10 USPTO Leader Profile Qualities; since Dec 2017 four sessions with 105 participants, 24 selected for supervisory positions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Non-Duty Hours Legal and Technical Studies reimbursement
rubrics_metrics.description: Programs to reimburse eligible employees for tuition at accredited law schools (legal) or for technical courses (technical) when courses are mission-related to increase knowledge and skills.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Non-Duty Hours Legal Studies supports JD degrees if mission-related (106 active participants in FY 2021, 100% tuition coverage); Technical Studies had 47 active participants in FY 2021.

rubrics_metrics.name: Patent Administrative Continued Education (PACE) and Upward Mobility Program (UMP)
rubrics_metrics.description: Programs to provide educational opportunities and career development for administrative staff and employees in positions with limited advancement options.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: PACE provided 19,808 hours to 695 participants in FY 2021; UMP had 112 active participants with 14,336 hours of training.

rubrics_metrics.name: Trademark examining attorney onboarding and mentorship
rubrics_metrics.description: Newly hired trademark examining attorneys typically receive six to eight weeks of classroom training (OTQRT and law office staff) and are then integrated into law offices where they are mentored by senior attorneys or paired with experienced examiners.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Training was conducted virtually in FY 2021 due to pandemic; law offices typically have ~25 attorneys across grade levels with mentoring structure defined.

rubrics_metrics.name: Trademark training content driven by quality review
rubrics_metrics.description: Trademark training materials and live/webcast modules are developed from analysis of quality review of Trademarks work products and cover targeted topics (e.g., TMEP updates, 2(d)/2(e)(1) office action writing, decision-making, ID/Class guidance, special marks, COVID-19/CBD resources).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Multiple training modules and guidance products (Examination Guides, Examination Notes, ID/Class Guidelines, Reminders) were released in FY 2021 to address topical issues and quality findings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Publication of examination guidance and ID/Class updates
rubrics_metrics.description: USPTO issues examination guides, examination notes, ID/Class guidelines, and bulletins (e.g., guidance on Generic.com after Booking.com, evidentiary standard for generic refusals, Brexit-affected US applications, Nice Classification 11th Ed. updates).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These publications clarify examination practice and classification policy; multiple releases and reminders were published across FY 2021 months.

rubrics_metrics.name: Statutory workload reporting (35 U.S.C. § 13)
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide the required FY workload tables and statistics as mandated by 35 U.S.C. § 13, including summaries of patent and trademark examining activities, application filings, pendency, dispositions, and related metrics.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The report includes numerous tables (Tables 1–29B) summarizing patent and trademark application and personnel statistics for FY periods.
